as: Pell Ambry: a wiry gnome wizard and retired locksmith, nosy, light-fingered and unfailingly polite
turns: I wander over to the water butt in the far corner of the yard and have a look behind it.
I get down on my knees and wriggle through the loose board into whatever is behind it.
I have a good look round up here, then lift the bar off the loft door and push it open so I can see down into the yard.
I pick up the smashed lantern from the floor and tuck it into my coat.
I lean out of the loft door and call down: "Sergeant! Up here, and mind the board behind the water butt, it's a squeeze."
I perch on the edge of the tally desk and wait for her, turning the lantern over in my hands.

as: Hal Brennick: a big, slow-spoken half-orc fighter, ex-docker, kind to children and terrible at whispering
turns: I walk over to the boy under the body, crouch down to his height and say, "Nice boots. Bit big for you, aren't they?"
I take a copper penny out and hold it up. "Swap you the penny for a look at the left boot. Just a look."
I put the penny in his palm and hold out my hand for the boot.
I turn the boot over, run my thumb along the lining and pick open the stitching where it crackles.
I hand the page to Kell to read, and give the boot back to the boy.
The girl on the wall looks ready to bolt. I step across to stand in the gateway, blocking it.

as: Sabine Marchetti: a brisk human cleric of the Lawgiver, former magistrate's clerk, allergic to nonsense
turns: I walk over to the yard wall and look up at the girl. "That's a nice bit of silver in your fist. Where does a wall-sitter get a wheat-ear crown?"
I reach up and pluck the coin out of her fingers before she can close them.
I hand the coin to Kell. "Evidence, Sergeant. Bag it."
"Sergeant, would you go to the palace and fetch the warden's key for these doors? I'll mind the yard."
I go and try the padlock on the granary's big yard doors.
I sit down on the cobbles with my back against the doors and wait.

as: Corvin Lark: a theatrical tiefling wizard who believes every problem is a stage that needs better lighting
turns: I climb up onto the yard wall and sit next to the girl, legs dangling.
I hop down into the lane, stroll to the far end of it, turn round and cast Fireball at the old elm.
I run back into the yard to the water butt, fill my hat and throw it over the burning branches hanging into the yard.
"Sergeant, help me tip the water butt over against the wall to soak the bottom of the tree!"
I check on the girl.

as: Oriel Vance: a fastidious elf wizard and former royal archivist who disapproves of everything
turns: I walk up to the bar, set a silver penny on the skiff hull and ask the landlady for a half measure of gossip.
I take my drink over to the champion's chair by the fire and sit in it.
"If anyone wants this chair back, they may ask nicely." I put my feet up on the corner of the card table.
I cast Fire Bolt at the eel traps hanging over the long table, to make a point about fire safety.
I point at the ale keg. "Well, don't just stand there, throw that on it!"
I stand up and bow to the room.

as: Hal Brennick: a big, slow-spoken half-orc fighter, ex-docker, kind to children and terrible at whispering
turns: I go and sit at the long table with the regulars and buy a round for the bench.
I stand up and challenge the big man in the corner to an arm-wrestle for the champion's chair, loud enough for the whole room.
I roll up my sleeve, sit down opposite him at the corner table and plant my elbow on it.
While everyone's watching the corner, I slip away into the scullery to look for the boy.
I open the slop hatch and look down at the river.
"Cob? It's all right, lad. Kell sent me. Come on out."

as: Nimby Fox: a halfling rogue with sticky fingers and a face like a choirboy
turns: I slip behind the skiff-hull bar while the landlady's back is turned and crouch down out of sight.
Still crouching, I find the jar marked FOREIGN, take out one of the heron pennies and pocket it.
I stand up, put the jar on the bar and say, "You've been taking foreign silver, Mrs Quill. Heron pennies."
I take Manners off its nails and hold it out to her, handle first. "Before you reach for it. I'm not here for a fight."
I walk over to the table by the door and sit down across from the man with the bandaged elbow.
